title: [ORION-QG QG-13 V4 / QG-9] All-n R6I support<=4 theorem via cumulative E2/E3 spectator-safe exchange
body:
Parent theorem miner: #767
Tightness theorem owner: #762
V2: #777 / PR #779
V3: #785 / PR #787
Canonical parent theorem: QG-1 wave-1 R6I support<=5

## Status

**CONFIRMATORY ALL-n THEOREM PACKET — exploratory evidence disclosed.**

After V3 was prospectively frozen, exploratory analysis showed that E2∪E3 covers all 216 five-column *fully accepting* support-five patterns. That is not sufficient for an all-n theorem because the partner generator may have additional active columns outside the selected support-five generator.

A subsequent exploratory spectator analysis identified the stronger theorem domain below: **324 anchored five-column slices** satisfying only the necessary conditions inherited from an arbitrary all-n QG-1-irreducible optimum. E2∪E3 covered 324/324 in exploratory analysis. Those numbers are used to formulate this confirmatory theorem and therefore are not treated as blind discovery.

V4 asks whether the ORION harnesses can independently machine-check the full all-n proof.

## Frozen base / execution identity

The implementation branch must be created from current ORION main after this issue is registered. No V2/V3 result code is imported into the analyzer; their action semantics are re-derived from production R6I tables. Parent QG-1 may be opened only as an already-earned theorem premise and receipt binding.

## Theorem target

> For every qubit count n and every instance of the frozen R6I two-block rank-2 dependent-triple shared-2-bit-Tag grammar under the frozen unit support objective, the exact optimum is attained with all four independent frame generators `RA0,RA1,RB0,RB1` of global support <=4.

Equivalently, `C_DP = C_cap4` for all n in the frozen R6I grammar.

## Proof skeleton

Choose a feasible configuration `Sigma` minimizing `(C,total_generator_support)` lexicographically over the finite unrestricted R6I search space.

### P1 — inherit QG-1 irreducibility/support<=5

QG-1's machine-checked SOLO/PAIR exchange theorem is an admitted parent premise. In a lexicographic minimum, no QG-1 move exists, so every generator has support <=5. V4 gives QG-1 full parent credit and does not re-claim support<=5.

### P2 — selected support-five slice

Suppose one independent generator `Rg` has support exactly five. Let `S=supp(Rg)`.

Outside S, `Rg=I`. Therefore the five columns in S carry **all** contributions to:
- `symp(Rg,Rother)=1` (anticommutation parity);
- the two shared-Tag syndrome bits of Rg, whose branch label is nonzero in every accepted R6I state.

The partner generator may have arbitrary additional columns outside S. Its Tag syndrome inside S therefore need not itself be an accepting label.

### P3 — necessary QG-1 irreducibility on the slice

Because Sigma has no QG-1 move:
- selected-generator non-coincidence N-classes inside S are zero-sum-free;
- coincidence C-classes inside S are zero-sum-free;
- partner-generator N-classes **restricted to S** are zero-sum-free (any zero-sum subset inside S would already be a valid global QG-1 move, regardless of additional partner-only columns outside S).

These are necessary conditions; V4 deliberately enumerates a superset of globally realizable support-five slices if outside-spectator constraints are ignored.

## Anchored-slice exhaustive lemma

Build local structural types directly from production R6I local tuples `(r0,r1,s0,s1)` and the inferred five-bit syndrome/action signatures.

For orientation g=0, enumerate every canonical multiset of exactly five columns with:
1. R0 active on all five columns;
2. XOR anticommutation bit = 1;
3. R0 two-bit Tag label !=0;
4. N0, restricted-N1 and C class multisets each have no nonempty zero-sum subset.

Do **not** require the slice's R1 Tag label to be accepted; outside R1-only spectator columns may complete it.

Repeat independently for orientation g=1 (R1 active on all five); do not assume symmetry without checking.

For each anchored slice, require at least one globally safe action from the cumulative frozen edit basis:
- E2: two distinct columns, actions A/B/AB, total five-bit syndrome change zero, exact summed worst local cost delta <=0;
- E3: three distinct columns, same conditions;
- action must delete at least one letter of the **selected support-five generator**.

Positive local lemma requires zero uncovered anchored slices in both orientations.

## Spectator-extension lemma

For every certified E2/E3 move on S:
- full five-bit block syndrome delta is exactly zero, so global anticommutation and both Tag labels are unchanged;
- actions only zero generator letters and recompute dependent R2 locally;
- Tag, targets, relative permutation, central choice, other block and all columns outside S are untouched;
- frozen R6I cost is a sum of per-column frame + Restore costs plus unchanged Tag/global constants, with **no cross-column Restore factor**;
- therefore the exact worst-case nonpositive local bound composes unchanged in the presence of arbitrary outside spectator columns.

The move deletes >=1 selected-generator letter, hence reduces support(Rg) from 5 to <=4 and strictly decreases total generator support. Cost does not increase. This contradicts lexicographic minimality.

Thus no generator in Sigma has support five; combined with QG-1 support<=5, every generator support<=4.

## Required machine checks

1. Production five-bit syndrome formula binds to R6I `_DELTA` exactly.
2. Recompute the complete single-column A/B/AB resource table and exact E2/E3 safe class sets; do not import V2/V3 result files.
3. Enumerate anchored-slice domains independently for g=0 and g=1.
4. Report exact counts, coverage split E2/E3/union, and any first uncovered pattern.
5. Verify every selected move deletes the chosen support-five generator.
6. Verify syndrome-zero composition and exact nonpositive worst cost.
7. Bind QG-1 parent receipt only after the anchored-slice lemma is sealed.
8. Independently reconstruct the entire anchored-slice lemma in generic ORION without importing production `_DELTA`.
9. Native ORION-Q must keep `LOCAL_LEMMA`, `SPECTATOR_EXTENSION`, and `ALL_N_THEOREM` obligations distinct; any missing obligation yields CANNOT_CHECK.

## Honest terminals

- `QG13V4_R6I_ALL_N_SUPPORT4_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG13V4_ANCHORED_SLICE_COUNTEREXAMPLE`
- `QG13V4_SPECTATOR_EXTENSION_GAP`
- `QG13V4_PARENT_BINDING_FAILED`
- `QG13V4_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Next boundary

A positive support<=4 theorem does not imply support four is tight. QG-9 must then reopen the tightness question at cap 3: exact support-4 witnesses or a stronger support<=3 exchange theorem.

## Novelty / authority boundary

Finite-field dependence, local exchange, dynamic programming, CEGIS and automated rewrite analysis are donor mathematics/methods. Candidate scientific contribution is only the frozen R6I all-n support<=4 normal-form theorem and its proof-carrying compiler instantiation. Novelty authority remains false pending independent external literature/peer review. No physical quantum-advantage claim.
